primary_metric.definition: bytes_missed / steps, aggregated exactly as argine.research2.r2_09a.fast_replay.run_fast already reports it per (trace, policy, budget) cell -- the same primary_physical_replay_quantity (miss_bytes) already frozen in experiments/R2-09-prediction-benchmark/metrics_contract.json.retention_metrics.
primary_metric.aggregation_rule: mean over the N BRIDGE-holdout instances of the per-instance miss_bytes_per_decode_step, equal weight per instance -- identical discipline to R2-09A's baseline-selection aggregation (never weighted by step/token count across instances, to prevent a longer trace dominating the average).

secondary_metrics: budget_violations (must be zero for every cell; a non-zero value is a correctness failure, not a scientific result)
comparator_relative_recovery_using_O_B_only_as_comparator (O_B is a comparator, never described as O*/optimal)

comparator_baseline.name: B_selected(M)
comparator_baseline.delta_definition: delta_miss_bytes_vs_b_selected = MissBytes(mechanism) - MissBytes(B_selected); negative is better for the mechanism (identical sign convention to metrics_contract.json).

outcomes.label: BRIDGE_NEGATIVE
outcomes.definition: At the primary budget (4 GiB), the aggregate (equal-weight-per-instance) miss_bytes_per_decode_step of every evaluated mechanism config is >= B_selected(M)'s -- i.e. no aggregate reduction versus B_selected at 4 GiB.

outcomes.label: BRIDGE_POSITIVE_BUT_WEAK
outcomes.definition: At least one mechanism config shows an aggregate reduction versus B_selected at 4 GiB (delta_miss_bytes_vs_b_selected < 0), but the improvement is NOT consistent: either it is negative (worse) for >=1 of the 4 BRIDGE-holdout workload instances, or it does not also show a non-positive aggregate delta at both secondary budgets (1.5 GiB and 8 GiB).

outcomes.label: BRIDGE_POSITIVE
outcomes.definition: At least one mechanism config shows an aggregate reduction versus B_selected at the primary 4 GiB budget (delta_miss_bytes_vs_b_selected < 0), the sign of that reduction is consistent (delta <= 0) across all 4 BRIDGE-holdout workload instances individually at 4 GiB, AND the improvement is not driven by a single workload (no single instance accounts for more than 3/4 of the total aggregate byte reduction).

decision_gate.tie_breaking_across_mechanism_configs: If multiple mechanism configs qualify for BRIDGE_POSITIVE, the config with the largest 4 GiB aggregate miss_bytes_per_decode_step reduction is reported as primary; all qualifying configs are reported, none are hidden.
decision_gate.no_post_hoc_thresholds: These three outcome definitions and their numeric/consistency criteria are frozen now, in Phase 0, before the BRIDGE holdout is captured or opened. No threshold may be added, removed, or adjusted after BRIDGE results exist.

relationship_to_r2_11: A BRIDGE_POSITIVE outcome may justify PROPOSING a new, separate R2-11 protocol prospectively. It never rewrites, and is not permitted to be interpreted as retroactively satisfying, the historical statement that R2-11 was NOT PROPOSED under the original frozen R2-10 decision rules (experiments/R2-10-working-set-predictor/decision_rules.json), which remains true and unchanged regardless of this bridge's outcome.

leakage_audit.method: Synthetic-trace future-alteration invariance: alter trace events strictly after a given decision boundary while holding the visible prefix identical; retention decisions (admission, eviction victim, resident set) up to and including that boundary must be bit-identical regardless of the alteration.

determinism_audit.method: Repeated replay with identical trace, predictor, policy, budget, and config must produce bit-identical scientific results (miss_bytes, misses, evictions, peak_resident_bytes, per-layer breakdown).

forbidden_claims_from_r2_bridge_01: runtime speedup or latency improvement (this is a replay-level feasibility question, not a runtime-speed question)
retention improvement beyond the 4 new BRIDGE-holdout instances actually evaluated
treating O_B (the comparator) as O* (the true offline optimum)
retroactive promotion of R2-10 Category B to Category C
retroactive reversal of the historical R2-11 NOT PROPOSED decision
use of the R2-10 EVAL set, in any form, as BRIDGE holdout or for BRIDGE policy tuning
